doc.title: Germaine Bazzle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006

title: Students surprised by her scatting
summary: A student was shocked to see her sing jazz; Rowe notes students realize later what they gained.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Right. Well I have a feeling that your students are very lucky to have you.

Oh thank you. It’s interesting because some of them don’t know that I do the jazz bit so we had — sometimes we have groups to come perform at the school and guys called me up one time to sing a song with them. And I started singing and started scatting and one of the students — and she sat that way for the entire song. And when we were finished she came to me and she says, “You fooled me, you fooled me, you don’t act like that in the classroom. Why you don’t act like that in the classroom?” I said, “It’s two different situations.” “You fooled me.” I said, “Okay, that was fun.”
That’s neat. Sometimes the impression you make on students is immediate and sometimes it’s years later that they realize what it was that they were getting from you.
True. And it is. Because they do come back and they tell you.
